en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ekacāriya Chapter on the Kuṭaja Flower: 9.
The Apadāna of the Elder Ekacāriya
“Among the Tāvatiṃsa devas,
a great cry then arose:
‘The Buddha has passed away into Nibbāna in the world!’”
And we ourselves are still possessed by passion.
For those who have thus become filled with spiritual urgency and are pierced by the arrow of sorrow—
Supported by Sabala,
he went into the presence of the Buddha,
taking a mandārava flower.
I performed the musical concert created by transformation,
which I offered to the Buddha at the time of his final nirvana.
All the gods rejoiced,
as did the celestial nymphs at that time;
for a hundred thousand eons,
I did not fall into an evil rebirth.
Sixteen people from among those [beings] sixty thousand eons ago from now—
The people known as the Great Mallas were wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) are...
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Ekacāriya Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Ekacāriya is the ninth.
